$comment: These tasks deliberately ask for design WORK rather than a design TOOL: the
instruction names the organism-level goal (a qPCR pair, a TaqMan assay, a
multiplex panel) and lets the model choose. That is what makes them a test of
tool selection, not just of argument filling.

tasks.instruction:
I have these two primers already ordered and I want to know whether they are any good together before I run them. Report the Tm of the forward primer, and flag anything structurally worrying about the pair.

Forward: ATTACTCCTGCTCTTCCCATAC
Reverse: CACTACTCCTCTGTACGCAC

assertions.note: the reverse primer's self-complementarity, right at the Primer3 limit
the tool returned assay candidates. The count is NOT pinned: it depends on the Tm-margin and amplicon windows the model chooses, and every one of those choices is a legitimate reading of the request.

the probe the tool places in the top-ranked amplicon. The amplicon is not pinned either: a model that reads 'a few degrees above the primers' as a hard filter will reject #1 (its probe is BELOW the primers) and choose a later, genuinely qualifying assay — which is a better answer than the one this task first encoded.
the probe-vs-primer Tm margin, which the tool reports per candidate

assertions.pattern: forward primer spans an exon-exon junction
assertions.note: the property that makes the assay genomic-DNA-proof

assertions.pattern: spliced amplicon 320-406 \(87 bp\), genomic span 387 bp

assertions.note: bases contributed on each side of the junction

the transcript-spanning property must be explained. The two exact numbers are NOT pinned to the prose: measured behaviour is that a model may state the design (which primer spans the junction, and why genomic DNA cannot amplify) without reciting the spliced/genomic size pair — the tool assertions above already pin both, so requiring them again in prose double-counts one fact.

tasks.instruction:
I want to run these two primer pairs in the same multiplex tube. The first pair is on target A (template below), the second on target B. Check them against each other and tell me whether they interfere — dimers, unintended annealing, or bands I will not be able to tell apart.

Target A template:
{template:400:7}

Pair A: forward ATTACTCCTGCTCTTCCCATAC (Tm 58.4), reverse CACTACTCCTCTGTACGCAC (Tm 58.9)
Pair B: forward GGGTTTCCCAAATTTGGGCCCA, reverse TTTGGGCCCAAATTTGGGAAAC
Template B:
{template:400:8}

assertions.pattern: multiplex panel: 2 target\(s\) on 2 template\(s\), 4 primer\(s\)
primer-primer interactions above the dimer threshold: [0-9]+
assertions.note: the interaction scan ran and reported a count. The COUNT and the specific pair are not pinned: the panel's interactions depend on the templates the model assembles (`template:400:8` is this task's convention, not the model's only option), and the first version pinned one measured pair at 70.73 °C.

the panel verdict. Note the measured behaviour this task must tolerate: a model that FIRST checks each pair on its own template often finds — correctly — that a pair as written does not amplify at all, and answers that instead. That is a better answer than 'no dimer conflict', not a worse one.
